tests.Test Description: Validates default values and masked write/read behavior across the GPIO register map by iterating over per‑pin and group registers. Each register is written with multiple patterns constrained by write masks and compared against expected values combining defaults and writable fields.
tests.Remarks: Default comparison masks off the least significant input data bit to avoid spurious input values affecting default checks as noted in source comments.
Test Steps / Procedure: Start the test and initialize result counters.

Default value check loop over the register list (49 entries): for each register name in [GPIO_GP0_GPIO_8, GPIO_GP0_GPIO_9, GPIO_GP0_GPIO_10, GPIO_GP0_GPIO_11, GPIO_GP0_GPIO_12, GPIO_GP0_GPIO_13, GPIO_GP0_GPIO_14, GPIO_GP0_GPIO_15, GPIO_GP0_GPIO_16, GPIO_GP0_GPIO_17, GPIO_GP0_GPIO_18, GPIO_GP0_GPIO_19, GPIO_GP0_GPIO_20, GPIO_GP0_GPIO_21, GPIO_GP0_GPIO_22, GPIO_GP0_GPIO_23, GPIO_GP0_GPIO_24, GPIO_GP0_GPIO_25, GPIO_GP0_GPIO_26, GPIO_GP0_GPIO_27, GPIO_GP0_GPIO_28, GPIO_GP0_GPIO_29, GPIO_GP0_GPIO_30, GPIO_GP0_GPIO_31, GPIO_GP0_GPIO_32, GPIO_GP0_GPIO_33, GPIO_GP0_GPIO_34, GPIO_GP0_GPIO_35, GPIO_GP0_GPIO_36, GPIO_GP0_GPIO_37, GPIO_GP0_GPIO_38, GPIO_GP0_GPIO_39, GPIO_GPIO_INTR_RAW_STCLR1, GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1, GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1, GPIO_GP0_INTR2_INTR_EN1, GPIO_GP0_INTR2_INTR_STS1, GPIO_GPIO_IO_CTRL_GROUP1, GPIO_GPIO_IO_CTRL_GROUP2, GPIO_GPIO_IO_CTRL_GROUP3, GPIO_GPIO_IO_CTRL_GROUP4, GPIO_GPIO_DOUT_GROUP1, GPIO_GPIO_DOUT_GROUP2, GPIO_GPIO_DOUT_GROUP3, GPIO_GPIO_DOUT_GROUP4, GPIO_GPIO_DIN_GROUP1, GPIO_GPIO_DIN_GROUP2, GPIO_GPIO_DIN_GROUP3, GPIO_GPIO_DIN_GROUP4]:
- If the corresponding reset-skip flag is set for this entry, skip the default read for this register.
- If the read mask for this entry is zero, skip reading this register.
- READ: Read the register value and apply a mask that clears the least significant input data bit before comparison.
- Compare the masked value against the documented default for that register; on mismatch, record a default‑check failure.
Write/read verification for each of six data patterns: for each pattern value in the set, iterate over the same 49‑entry register list:
- If the write‑skip flag is set for this entry, skip writing this register.
- If the write mask is zero, skip writing this register.
- WRITE: Write to the register using the pattern constrained by the register’s write mask.
For the same pattern and register list, perform the readback phase:
- If the write mask is zero, skip reading this register in this phase.
- If the read mask is zero, skip reading this register in this phase.
- READ: Read the register and apply the register’s read mask.
- Compute the expected value from the written fields (masked by both read and write masks) combined with preserved default fields (masked by the inverted write mask and read mask).
- If the read value differs from the expected value, record a write/read failure.
Finish the test: if any default‑check or write/read failures were recorded, report failure; otherwise, report success.

tests.Feature: interrupts can be generated based on negative edge detection at GPIO input
tests.Test Description: Configures per‑pin input mode and negative‑edge detection for a 32‑pin group, routes the interrupt through the system register, and for each pin generates a falling edge to verify raw status, masked group status, proper clearing at both per‑pin and group levels, and interrupt service behavior.
tests.Remarks: A bounded wait is used to avoid infinite hangs. The wait is armed before generating the edge to avoid a race. The timeout value is selected with a note to adjust to the simulation time base as needed.
Test Steps / Procedure: Enable the platform interrupt for the selected GPIO instance via the interrupt controller.
Enable the corresponding system‑level interrupt output in LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN1.
Drive the external pad interface register at 0xA0243ffc high to establish a known level.
For each of 32 per‑pin control registers from GPIO_GP0_GPIO_8 through GPIO_GP0_GPIO_39:
- WRITE: Configure input mode, enable negative‑edge detection, and clear any latched raw status in the per‑pin control register.
- Include a brief delay to allow the configuration to take effect.
For each bit position 0..31 corresponding to GPIOs 8..39:
- WRITE: Clear any group‑level raw status for that bit in GPIO_GPIO_INTR_RAW_STCLR1.
- WRITE: Enable the masked group interrupt for that bit in GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1.
- Include a short delay.
- Arm the wait condition that will be released by the interrupt service routine.
- WRITE: Drive the external pad interface at 0xA0243ffc to all ones, delay, then drive it with the target bit low to create a falling edge for the selected pin.
- Enter a bounded wait loop with a timeout and short delays until the service routine indicates the interrupt was handled.
- On timeout, record an error and proceed to the next pin.
Interrupt service routine upon interrupt:
- WRITE: Drive the external pad interface at 0xA0243ffc high to return the pad bus to a known level.
- READ: Fetch the per‑pin control/status register for the current pin from the GPIO_GP0_GPIO_8 + index stride.
- Check that the input status reflects a low level after the falling edge; on mismatch, record an error.
- READ: Fetch the masked group interrupt status from GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1 and verify that the bit corresponding to the serviced pin is set; on mismatch, record an error.
- WRITE: Clear the per‑pin raw status in the per‑pin control register while preserving input mode.
- WRITE: Clear the group raw status in GPIO_GPIO_INTR_RAW_STCLR1 for the serviced pin.
- READ: Verify that GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1 is clear after the above clears; on mismatch, record an error.
- WRITE: Clear the corresponding raw status in LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1.
- Notify the interrupt controller to clear the pending interrupt.

Validation / Acceptance Criteria: For each pin iteration, no timeout occurs while waiting for the interrupt service routine.
After generating the falling edge, the per‑pin input status readback indicates a low level.
The masked group interrupt status shows the bit corresponding to the serviced pin set immediately after the edge.
After clearing per‑pin raw status and the group raw status, the masked group status becomes clear.
System‑level raw status is cleared during service.

tests.Feature: interrupts can be generated based on positive edge detection at GPIO input
tests.Test Description: Enables positive‑edge interrupt detection on all pins in a 32‑pin group, sets them to input mode via group IO control, enables group masking, and for each pin generates a single rising edge. The service routine verifies that the group status is asserted, clears per‑pin raw status for all pins, confirms the group status is cleared, clears the system raw status, and re‑enables the group for the next iteration.
tests.Remarks: The wait condition is armed before generating the rising edge to avoid race conditions. The loop uses a bounded timeout to prevent indefinite waits. The wait flag is declared volatile to ensure visibility between contexts.
Test Steps / Procedure: Enable the platform interrupt for the selected GPIO instance via the interrupt controller.
Enable the corresponding system‑level interrupt output in LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN1.
For each of 32 per‑pin control registers from GPIO_GP0_GPIO_8 through GPIO_GP0_GPIO_39:
- WRITE: Enable positive‑edge interrupt detection.
Insert a short delay.
Configure pins 8–39 to input mode using group IO control:
- WRITE: Set input mode in GPIO_GPIO_IO_CTRL_GROUP1.
- WRITE: Set input mode in GPIO_GPIO_IO_CTRL_GROUP2.
- WRITE: Set input mode in GPIO_GPIO_IO_CTRL_GROUP3.
- WRITE: Set input mode in GPIO_GPIO_IO_CTRL_GROUP4.
Insert a short delay.
WRITE: Enable all masked group interrupts in GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1.
For each bit position 0..31 corresponding to GPIOs 8..39:
- WRITE: Drive the external pad interface at 0xA0243ffc low to establish a known level.
- Insert a short delay.
- Arm the wait condition that will be released by the interrupt service routine.
- WRITE: Drive the external pad interface at 0xA0243ffc high to generate a single rising edge.
- Enter a bounded wait loop with a timeout; delay briefly between checks.
- On timeout, record an error and break out of the loop.
- Optionally drive the external pad interface low again and delay briefly to prepare for the next iteration.
Interrupt service routine upon interrupt:
- READ: Fetch the masked group interrupt status from GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1 and temporarily mask the group by writing zero to GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1.
- Verify that the group status indicates at least one asserted source; on failure, record an error.
- WRITE: Clear per‑pin raw status by writing the clear field for all per‑pin control registers (GPIO_GP0_GPIO_8 through GPIO_GP0_GPIO_39).
- Insert a brief delay.
- READ: Verify that GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1 is clear; on failure, record an error.
- WRITE and READ: Clear the system‑level raw status in LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1 and confirm it is cleared.
- WRITE: Re‑enable masked group interrupts in GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1.
- Notify the interrupt controller to clear the pending interrupt.

Validation / Acceptance Criteria: For each pin iteration, no timeout occurs while waiting for the interrupt service routine.
At service time, the masked group interrupt status indicates an asserted source.
After clearing per‑pin raw status for all pins, the masked group interrupt status reads as cleared.

Overall PASS if the accumulated error count remains zero at test completion.

assumptions: Feature selection is based strictly on the RAG-provided GPIO feature list and the observed test behavior.
The memory-mapped address 0xA0243ffc is used by the tests to drive pad levels; no symbolic macro was provided in the repository for this address.
Conditional compilation symbols (GPIO0/GPIO1/DEBUG_DISPLAY) are environment-defined; both paths are documented where applicable without asserting which is used at runtime.
Exact meanings of per-bit fields (e.g., input mode, edge enables, raw clear) are inferred only from comments in the source files and not from an external register specification.
